{"name":"pr4g/vvar-advances","commit":{"sha":"d4763907230ca6dd097b797e4b1c68973af6bb72","node_id":"C_kwDOAORW-9oAKGQ0NzYzOTA3MjMwY2E2ZGQwOTdiNzk3ZTRiMWM2ODk3M2FmNmJiNzI","commit":{"author":{"name":"Benedikt Stebner","email":"Gillibald@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-09-07T07:53:53Z"},"committer":{"name":"Benedikt Stebner","email":"Gillibald@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-09-29T13:47:42Z"},"message":"Add the variation advance-lookup benchmark

Covers the three shapes that matter for the variation work: a static
font, a variable font at its default instance, and a varied clone, each
at 1 / 20 / 200 / 2000 glyphs, with Skia's GetGlyphWidths as the baseline
in both its widths-only and widths-plus-bounds call shapes. Shared
typeface loaders and glyph-index arrays live in VariationFixtures so the
measured region is the lookup itself.

Iteration counts are raised above BenchmarkDotNet's defaults for the
single-glyph variants; at sub-2ns those measurements are otherwise
dominated by timer noise.

This is the harness behind the region-scaler numbers quoted in the two
commits below it, and the guard that keeps static and default-instance
callers from silently regressing as more variation tables are wired in.
